items.name: Hydrogen
items.fact: Liquid hydrogen fuels many rocket upper stages.

items.name: Nitrogen
items.fact: Liquid nitrogen is used to make 'instant' ice cream.

items.name: Oxygen
items.fact: Liquid oxygen is pale blue and magnetic.

items.name: Mercury
items.fact: Mercury thermometers can measure up to about 350 °C.

items.name: Sulfur
items.fact: Sulfur has been known since ancient times as brimstone.

items.name: Zinc
items.fact: Zinc boils at a lower temperature than copper melts.

items.name: Lead
items.fact: Lead boils at a temperature hotter than lava from many volcanoes.

items.name: Aluminium
items.fact: Aluminium stays liquid across a range of almost 1,800 °C.

items.name: Copper
items.fact: Copper vapor lasers produce yellow and green light.

items.name: Iron
items.fact: Iron vapor has been detected in the atmosphere of a scorching exoplanet.

items.name: Gold
items.fact: Gold can be beaten so thin that light shines through it.

items.name: Titanium
items.fact: Titanium is named after the Titans of Greek mythology.

items.name: Tungsten
items.fact: Tungsten boils at about the temperature of the Sun's surface.
